statement: src/unitOperations/distillation/RateBasedSegment.cpp:782, :849 and :751-755: a reboiler composition with one component at zero is accepted at exit 0 with the energy closure 'verified'.  ratebased01 with pXylene 0: HETP 0.0127579629 m published (0.1555825 m with the case's 0.2), built from a reflux composition of 3.4e-27; with oXylene 0: HETP NaN, printed '-nan m', the result's HETP null.  The 1 % discretisation refusal compares with `>` and cannot fire on NaN.  Reproduced by the reviewing session (both).

src/unitOperations/distillation/RateBasedSegment.cpp:572-574, :791-794, :1003: the column's first-law check sums to Q_cond + Q_reb,own = -(reference latent heat) x the sum of the interface energy row; whatever the two film energy terms contain cancels.  It verifies that the three energy rows were solved, not the interface physics; its stated blind spot names only the split between the two duties.  Gap 1.7e-13 kW against a tolerance of 1.1e-5 on all four cases.

The limit agreement (0.0025 to 0.016 %) is two discretisations of one equation through the same correlation functions and property calls (src/unitOperations/distillation/RateBasedSegment.cpp:383-420 against DistillationColumn.cpp:5600-5640): it proves the reduction, the wiring and second order, and is no evidence about the non-equilibrium model.  The guide says so.
check_ratebased_segment.py arm (1): the tolerance (0.83 to 1.74 %) is 70 to 430 times looser than the measured difference; a defect in the limit path moving the HETP by under about 1 % passes.

The gate's non-ideal-liquid arm runs UNIFAC on p- and o-xylene, which have identical groups, so every activity coefficient is exactly 1: the arm tests the announcement and no non-ideal number (all KPIs equal to the ideal run within 1e-10).

src/unitOperations/distillation/RateBasedSegment.cpp:448: the liquid thermal conductivity feeds the liquid film's heat-transfer coefficient and is absent from the run's property-sources table and from the goldens' source rows.

RateBasedSegment.H:129-132 says the discretisation refusal is r_max squared over 12; the code uses a Richardson estimate.  At 10 segments the header's rule would refuse (0.18) and the run is accepted (0.29 %).

Inputs refused without being named: height 0 ('non-finite Jacobian column 0'), a negative height ('Newton did not converge'), a negative pressure (an equation-of-state volume message); `segments 10.7` is silently truncated to 10.

src/unitOperations/distillation/RateBasedSegment.cpp:341-342: a formation-enthalpy probe at a hard-coded 350 K raises the caveat block's extrapolation lines; on ratebased02 the bed runs at 307.8 to 314.5 K, wholly below one component's liquid heat-capacity range (315 to 418 K), and the caveat names the probe's temperature, not the states used.

On main before this slice too: `feed F1;` written at unit level is stripped as a wire key before the unit sees it (UnitInputs.cpp:116), so the model's refusal of a feed cannot fire; exit 0, identical KPIs, no audit line.
src/unitOperations/distillation/RateBasedSegment.cpp:309: a comment calls the pure-component interface enthalpies exact for 'the only phases this slice accepts'; a non-ideal liquid is accepted.

The +0.03 to +0.19 % beyond the limit is at equal REBOILER load; at equal bed-mean load, the abscissa of the measured comparison, the two models differ by -0.015 to +0.009 % on the first case.  Most of the +0.19 % is the vapour growing 0.9 % up the bed, not interface physics; a reader can attribute it wrongly.

WilkeChang.cpp:48: the comment says the record's volume is at the boiling point; these records give it at 298 K.  With the boiling-point volume the liquid diffusivity falls 7.6 % and H_OG at mid-bed rises 0.72 %.  Shared with the transfer-unit bed; the run announces the 25 C volume.
The guide's table against the measurement is regenerated by no tool and does not state which load it uses; (top + bottom)/2 reproduces every digit.
On main before this slice too: the plant-boundary energy report says 'this plant declares no duty' (Q_heat 0) for a column exchanging 410 kW each way.
